title: AvePoint and Google Workspace: Meeting Migration Requirements Together
summary: Plan your Google Workspace migration strategy using Google native capabilities and AvePoint tools for secure, AI-ready collaboration and seamless governance.
body_markdown:
Google Workspace adoption continues to grow as organizations modernize their collaboration environments and prepare for new AI-enabled ways of working.[Gartner projects](https://www.gartner.com/en/documents/7472826) that through 2030, the number of organizations migrating to Google Workspace will triple annually as they seek to take advantage of new AI capabilities. As adoption accelerates, effective migration strategies extend moving data: They ensure the entire organization can operate seamlessly in Google Workspace. While Google ’


s native migration covers primary workloads such as email, calendars, contacts, and standard file repositories, additional considerations often emerge around governance, business continuity, collaboration context, stakeholder visibility, and long-term data resilience.


For many organizations, that means using Google ’


s native migration tools as the foundation while leveraging AvePoint ’


s complementary capabilities to support broader migration, governance, resilience, and operational requirements.


## Start with Requirements, Not Migration Tools


Migration planning often begins with evaluating products and features. A more effective approach is to first define what success should look like after the transition is complete.


Before selecting a migration path, define:


- Which content to preserve — and at what fidelity.
- What collaboration experiences users rely on today.
- What governance and compliance requirements must continue after migration.
- What business processes depend on migrated content.
- What visibility stakeholders need throughout the project.
- What success should look like after cutover.


These discussions uncover varies workload requirements. Some organizations may prioritize moving content quickly and efficiently. Others may be focused on preserving collaboration experiences, supporting regulatory obligations, maintaining business continuity, or establishing governance from day one.


Moving content is only part of the challenge. The real measure of success is whether employees can continue to collaborate, access information, and deliver business outcomes once the transition is complete.


## Where Google ’


s Native Migration Capabilities Deliver Value


Google ’


s native migration capabilities provide an important foundation for organizations moving to Google Workspace. They help migrate core workloads, establish migration plans, and accelerate the transition to a modern collaboration environment.


Google offers native migration tools for Exchange, OneDrive, SharePoint, and Teams — covering core workloads like email, calendars, contacts, files, and collaboration experiences. Google has also expanded migration planning capabilities through[Google Migration Planner](https://github.com/google/migration-planner) , helping organizations assess migration scope and organize migration waves before execution begins.


For straightforward projects, these capabilities may fully support the transition.


These capabilities form a strong baseline for migration success. As migration requirements evolve, many organizations evaluate how complementary capabilities can help support additional requirements related to collaboration preservation, governance, resilience, operational visibility, and long-term information management.

The right mix depends on migration complexity and business requirements. Regardless of the approach, data resilience should be part of the conversation from the start. Planning for recovery before cutover helps organizations reduce risk and maintain business continuity long after the migration is complete.


## Build the Migration Strategy That Fits the Work


Organizations planning a Google Workspace migration no longer need to think in terms of native capabilities versus third-party solutions.


Google ’


s native migration capabilities and AvePoint ’


s capabilities are often most effective when evaluated together as part of a broader migration strategy.


The key question isn ’


t which tool does the task. It is whether the overall strategy supports the business outcomes the organization is trying to achieve. The organizations that realize the most value from Google Workspace are the ones that start with their business requirements rather than specific tools. They combine Google ’


s native capabilities with complementary capabilities needed to support successful outcomes before, during, and after migration.
